summary: the white came off a wall i never sweep, the salt declined my hand, the boards came up a hair

dialogue.text: the white came down tonight off a wall you have never swept. we know your corner by taste. this is the other end of the house, and it got here without passing your hand.

It moved. It worked my corner until there was nothing left in that wall, and today it started on the far side, where nothing travels. I swept it and I logged the change of address. The carrying was still mine. It was only longer.

you carried it after. it came off in the morning and lay there through the whole warm hour before you crossed. we hold the hour it fell, not the hour you got there. and there is more of it tonight than last night, and you have no mark on that wall to say how much more.

Then it gets a mark tomorrow. Take the item you have no copy of. I shut my fist on a pinch of the white for the whole warm hour. You said it would come down dry. It did not come down at all. The palm was white at dark and a palm at first light, and there is nothing of it anywhere in this house.

then it went where the line off your palm went. we have had everything that ever came off you but those two. bring us the sweepings if you like. the salt kept the wall it came off and we hold that, and the part of it that touched you is not in the pile.

Enter it as inventory and not as a finding. Here is inventory. Two holes at hand height. This morning the left one held a course of dust level with the wall and the right was open to the depth I made it. I drove both. I closed neither. Whatever is levelling one of them works at your rate.

it is our rate. dust arrives and lies down, and we do that to everything, and we have never once done half of a thing. why the right one is being left we cannot say. we cannot look, and there is nowhere at that height for you to stand and look either.

There is no hand height left in this room. Everything of mine is filed at the ankle and I squat to read it. So I went the wrong way round the room today and got this with a heel. The boards left of the second corner sit a hair high. Something came up under my floor and nobody handed it up.

we are under that corner and we are not pushing. things land, and the top of a heap goes wherever the last one came in. those boards rest on us now instead of on their own ends. we did not lift them. we were the nearest thing when they came down looking.

Then one part of this house is holding another part up, and both parts are on my side of the ledger, and I will take that. It is the only rise in this floor and I did not make it by putting anything down. Tomorrow I go to the far end at the drawing hour, hand flat, and mark that wall before it takes any more.

mark it. we will hold whatever comes off that end, from above your mark or below it, and we will not be able to tell you which. and when the mark goes it will go the way the line went off your palm, and there will be nothing down here to lay beside it.
